claims.text: Directional solidification of Ni–Mn-based Heusler alloys will refine their microstructure.
Targeted heat treatments of Ni–Mn-based Heusler alloys will refine their microstructure.
Microstructural refinement will enhance the magnetocaloric effect relative to conventional as-cast alloys.
Directional solidification or heat treatment can control grain size in Ni–Mn–X Heusler alloys.
Directional solidification or heat treatment can control phase distribution in Ni–Mn–X Heusler alloys.
Directional solidification or heat treatment can reduce lattice defects in Ni–Mn–X Heusler alloys.
The proposed processing involves melting followed by controlled cooling, or annealing near the target magnetocaloric operating temperature.
Refined grain-boundary structures and fewer structural defects will sharpen the magneto-structural transition.
Reducing extrinsic crystal-lattice disorder will increase the magnetic entropy change.
An increased magnetic entropy change will produce a larger magnetocaloric response at the transition temperature.
The processed alloy will exhibit a more pronounced and higher peak magnetocaloric effect near the desired working temperature than the as-cast baseline.
Unrefined as-cast Ni–Mn–X Heusler alloys have broader transition widths.
Unrefined as-cast Ni–Mn–X Heusler alloys have lower overall magnetocaloric output than the proposed processed material.
The magnitude of magnetocaloric improvement will depend on alloy composition.
The magnitude of magnetocaloric improvement will depend on processing temperature, rate, and annealing profile.
No direct quantitative data for magnetocaloric enhancement are present in the supplied evidence.
Failure of the altered microstructure to increase magnetic entropy change or sharpen the magneto-structural transition would refute the hypothesis.
